lesson.title: Containers from Zero, part 8: configuration and the database file
lesson.description: Move the notes app's settings into a .env file, give PostgreSQL a named volume so notes survive down and up, change configuration without rebuilding, and make a backup that you restore into an empty database to prove it works.
lesson.tested: Ran the .env, volume and backup steps with Compose v5.8.0 and Engine 29.10.1, 25 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: A named volume keeps the notes; a backup counts once you have restored it into an empty database.

boards.note: `POSTGRES_*` variables only set up an empty volume. Changing the password later needs `\password notes` in psql inside the database.

steps.title: What the lab showed
steps.hint: IDs and times differ on your machine

items.what: `required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing a value: set it in .env`.
`notes_db-data` stayed and both notes came back.
`backup.sql`, 98 lines, with the notes in its `COPY` block.
After `down -v`, `pg_isready` said `no response`, then `accepting connections`; `psql` read the file and the notes returned.

steps.note: Safety: publishes 127.0.0.1:8080. Step 6 runs `docker compose down -v`, which deletes the database volume; run it only after the backup shows your notes. Undo with `docker compose down -v` and delete `.env` and `backup.sql`.

commands.cmd: docker compose exec db pg_dump -U notes notes > backup.sql
until docker compose exec db pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U notes -d notes; do sleep 1; done
docker compose exec -T db psql -q -U notes -d notes < backup.sql

homework.intro: Use the notes folder from the lesson. IDs and times will differ. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What is the difference between `${APP_TITLE:-Notes}` and `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set it in .env}`?
exercises.a: The first uses `Notes` when the variable is unset or empty. The second makes Compose stop with `set it in .env`.

exercises.q: Where must the `.env` file be, and what wins over it?
exercises.a: Next to compose.yaml, in the project directory. Shell variables win, and `--env-file` replaces it.

exercises.q: What does Docker's guide say about passwords in environment variables?
exercises.a: Don't use environment variables to pass sensitive information such as passwords; use secrets instead.

exercises.q: Where is the named volume mounted for PostgreSQL 18, and what is `PGDATA`?
Why must the database exist before `psql` reads `backup.sql`?
exercises.a: Restoring with `psql` does not create the database. Here the image creates `notes` on the empty volume first.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose config` with no `.env` file. What happens, and why?
exercises.a: Two `required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing a value` errors, one for `db` and one for `DATABASE_URL`: the `:?` form stops Compose.

exercises.q: Change `APP_TITLE` in `.env` and run `docker compose up -d`. Which containers change?
exercises.a: `notes-web-1` is recreated from the same image; `notes-db-1` stays `Running`. No build runs.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose down`, `docker volume ls --filter name=notes`, `docker compose up -d`. Are the notes there?
exercises.a: Yes. `notes_db-data` survives `down`, and the new `db` container mounts it again.

exercises.q: Run the `pg_isready` loop right after `docker compose up -d db` on an empty volume. What does it print?
exercises.a: `no response` one or more times, then `accepting connections`, when it exits 0 and the loop ends.

exercises.q: Run `APP_TITLE="From the shell" docker compose up -d`, then plain `docker compose up -d`. What title does each show?
exercises.a: `From the shell`, then the `.env` value again. The shell variable applied to one run.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You change `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in `.env` after the volume has a database, then run `up -d`. What happens?
exercises.a: `web` gets `password authentication failed`; `db` logs `Skipping initialization`. Put the old value back or change it with psql `\password notes`.

exercises.q: You restore `backup.sql` into the running database that still has the notes. What do you see?
exercises.a: `ERROR:  relation "notes" already exists` and a duplicate key error; nothing is restored. Use an empty volume.

exercises.q: You mount the volume at `/var/lib/postgresql/data` on PostgreSQL 18. Do notes survive `down` and `up`?
exercises.a: No notes at all: `db` exits with code 1 and an `Error: in 18+` message naming `/var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)`. Mount at `/var/lib/postgresql`.

exercises.q: You run `docker compose down -v` before making a backup. Can you get the notes back?
exercises.a: No. `down -v` deletes `notes_db-data` and the notes with it.
